questions.question: The distance from the centre of a circle to any point on its boundary is called the:
questions.explanation: Radius = distance from centre to boundary. Diameter = 2 × radius (passes through centre). Chord = line joining any two points on the boundary (doesn't need to pass through centre).

A bicycle wheel has diameter 70 cm. How many rotations does it make to travel 110 m? (π = 22/7; 110 m = 11,000 cm)
questions.explanation: Circumference = πd = (22/7) × 70 = 220 cm. Rotations = Total distance ÷ Circumference = 11,000 ÷ 220 = 50.

questions.question: Which has a greater circumference: Circle A (radius 7 cm) or Circle B (diameter 15 cm)? (π = 22/7)
questions.explanation: C(A) = 2×(22/7)×7 = 44 cm. C(B) = π×15 = (22/7)×15 ≈ 47.1 cm. Circle B has the greater circumference.

questions.question: The circumference of a circle equals the perimeter of a square with side 11 cm. Radius of the circle (π = 22/7) =
questions.explanation: Perimeter of square = 4 × 11 = 44 cm. Circumference = 44 → 2πr = 44 → 2 × (22/7) × r = 44 → r = 44 × 7/44 = 7 cm.

questions.question: Arc vs Circumference: The arc PQ is half the circumference of a circle with radius 10 cm. Arc length PQ (π = 22/7) =
If the radius of a circle is doubled, its circumference:
questions.explanation: C = 2πr. If r → 2r, then C → 2π(2r) = 4πr = 2 × (2πr). Circumference doubles when radius doubles. (Compare: area quadruples when radius doubles.)

questions.question: A wire of length 88 cm is bent into a circle. Radius of the circle (π = 22/7) =
questions.explanation: Wire length = circumference = 88 cm. 2πr = 88 → 2 × (22/7) × r = 88 → (44/7) × r = 88 → r = 88 × 7/44 = 14 cm.
